items.title: Pakistan conducted strikes at 10 locations in Afghanistan in response to recent drone attacks: info minister
items.description: Pakistan has conducted precision aerial and drone strikes in 10 locations across Afghanistan in retaliation for drones launched from the neighbouring country a day earlier, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said in the early hours of Thursday. “In exercise of its sovereign right to self-defence, Pakistan conducted precision aerial and drone strikes against 10 locations in Afghanistan used for launching and storing these drones,” Tarar wrote in a post on social media platform X. He added that the strikes were “deliberate, precise, calibrated and proportionate, and strictly limited to identified military objectives directly linked to the attempted attacks against Pakistan”. In the post, Tarar condemned Wednesday’s “deliberate and unlawful” drone incursion, calling it a “blatant violation of Pakistan’s sovereignty and territorial integrity”. He held the drone attacks were a “grave and unacceptable act of aggression”. The information minister said Pakistan had conveyed its concerns to the Afghan Taliban over the terrorist elements emanating from Afghan soil and the presence of terrorist sanctuaries. However, he noted that rather than dismantling the terrorist networks and taking action against them, the Afghan Taliban chose to “escalate the situation through hostile drone operations against Pakistan”. He said that in Wednesday’s attack, Pakistan’s air defence systems had “detected, tracked and neutralised all intruding platforms before they could reach any of their intended targets, comprehensively thwarting the attempted attack”. Tarar held that Pakistan will “neither accept nor tolerate” attacks from Afghan territory — whether by terrorist groups or the Afghan Taliban regime itself. He warned against violation of Pakistan’s sovereignty, vowing that it will be met with “an immediate and decisive response”. The minister further held that: “Any threats, denials or attempts to deflect responsibility by [the] Afghan Taliban will neither alter the facts nor constrain Pakistan’s inherent right to defend its territory, its people and its national security.” Tarar, in the post, called upon the regime in Kabul to halt immediately “hostile activity” and abide by international obligations “by taking effective, concrete, verifiable and sustained action against terrorist entities operating from Afghan soil”. The minister warned that the Afghan territory should not be used for attacks against Pakistan. He maintained that Pakistan remained committed to “regional peace, dialogue and constructive engagement” and was not seeking escalation. However, the information minister warned: “This commitment must not be mistaken for weakness or an unlimited tolerance of hostile actions”. He also vowed that the country will defend its sovereignty, territorial integrity and the lives of citizens with “full resolve and take all necessary measures to protect them”. “Any further provocative act by [the] Afghan Taliban will be responded with [a] firm and resolute response,” the information minister warned. In another post, the minister shared footage of the aerial and drone strikes. “These targets were linked to terrorist attacks inside Pakistan against unarmed civilians and recent foiled drone intrusion by Afghan Taliban regime on Sept 23,” he said. “Pakistan will continue to defend its territorial integrity and protect lives and properties of its citizens against any externally sponsored, sheltered and abetted threat by terrorist proxies,” Tarar said. Pakistan’s response came after eight drones, launched from Afghanistan, entered Pakistani airspace near the Torkham border and Kohat on Wednesday. Security sources said they were subsequently shot down. It was also reported that the Afghan Taliban engaged in unprovoked firing the night before near Kurram as security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Pakistan. On Sept 21, Pakistan, in response to recent terrorist attacks in KP, conducted “calibrated” airstrikes in the border region with Afghanistan against terrorist hideouts and safe havens of terrorist organisations. A statement from the information ministry on Monday said that over 28 terrorists were eliminated in the strikes. “It is a matter of grave concern that Afghanistan continues to remain a hub of terrorism,” the ministry said at the time, specifying that the “threat to Pakistan emanates from Afghanistan”. The airstrikes had come after a major attack in the old Police Lines in KP’s Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation launched to clear the area. Ghazab lil Haq Tarar described Pakistan’s action as part of its ongoing counter-terrorism campaign, Ghazab lil Haq. On the night of February 26, following unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban from across the border, Pakistan launched Operation Ghazab lil Haq against terrorist hideouts. Pakistan also carried out strikes in the border region with Afghanistan in late June , with the government saying they were in response to a wave of terrorist attacks, including one on a Rangers camp in Karachi . At the time, Tarar said that 25 terrorists were killed in those strikes in Paktia, Paktika and Kunar. Pakistan had carried out similar strikes on terrorist hideouts along its border with Afghanistan earlier that month, killing 26 terrorists. In July, security forces responded to unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban at border posts in Kurram, security sources had said. In the same month, the Afghan Taliban regime launched four rudimentary drones across the border into Balochistan, which were shot down by security forces. Two drones were also shot down in June in Qila Abdullah and Chagai districts. Pak-Afghan ties As clashes continue, tensions between Islamabad and Kabul have remained high. Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned TTP, that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded. Earlier this week, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar addressed a meeting of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), where he called for steps towards concrete and verifiable action to prevent the use of Afghan soil for terrorism against any neighbouring country, particularly Pakistan. Dar said Pakistan was “seriously concerned” about the presence of over two dozen terrorist groups in Afghanistan that threatened regional and international peace and security. Last week, Pakistan also told the UN Security Council that it would respond to terrorist threats emanating from Afghanistan in self-defence as and when needed and in accordance with international law. Earlier this month, the Foreign Office (FO) declared that meaningful progress in relations with Kabul would depend on the Taliban taking concrete and verifiable action against Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and other terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory. It maintained that while Islamabad welcomed China’s continuing engagement, the external facilitation could not substitute for action by Kabul against terrorist infrastructure. According to a UN Security Council-mandated monitoring report — covering the period from December 16, 2025 to June 9, 2026 — Afg­han Taliban’s continued support for TTP has contributed to a rise in the frequency and lethality of terrorist attacks in Pakistan, even as Kabul has taken some initial steps to rein in the group. The report also pointed to growing operational and facilitation linkages among the TTP, Al Qaeda, Islamic State-Khorasan (ISIL-K) and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA).

items.title: Tallal warns proposed changes to KP police law could 'weaken' command structure
items.description: Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry on Thursday criticised the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government’s proposed law to replace the KP Police Act, 2017, warning that changes to the police command structure could affect the force’s ability to maintain law and order and fight terrorism. The KP government on Wednesday approved a proposed law to replace the KP Police Act, 2017, curtailing the powers of the inspector general of police (IGP) by making the police chief’s operational, administrative and financial decisions subject to approval from the provincial government or chief minister. Addressing the media in Islamabad, Chaudhry said policing and the maintenance of public order were primarily provincial subjects under the constitutional framework established by the 18th Amendment, but provinces did not have unlimited powers to legislate beyond the Constitution and existing legal frameworks. He said the Police Service of Pakistan (PSP) rules and other relevant laws provided the framework governing the police and could not be overridden through provincial legislation. “You cannot change the command structure of a police force that is fighting terrorism, losing its personnel every day, and continuing to perform its duties and make sacrifices despite limited resources, through legislation that is inconsistent with Pakistan’s Constitution and the PSP rules,” he said. “You cannot use such legislation to structurally dismantle its command structure.” The minister said the proposed law did not merely curtail the powers of the IGP but “dismantled the entire command structure”. He said the proposed law would also strip regional police officers, who are deputy inspectors general (DIGs), of the authority to appoint grade-17 officers, including deputy superintendents of police (DSPs), while additional inspectors general would no longer be able to make appointments to grade-17, 18 and 19 posts that were not field postings. “How can one person take all these powers into their own hands?” he asked, alleging that Chief Minister Sohail Afridi was seeking to bring the entire system under his “personal and political control”. Chaudhry also questioned whether police officers would continue to take decisions on professional grounds if the command structure was weakened, warning that the move could affect “discipline and morale within the force”. Referring to the chief minister’s authority over postings, he said all four chief ministers had limited powers in this regard, but these did not affect the police command structure. He also questioned why the provincial government had not introduced the proposed legislation earlier if changes to the 2017 law were considered necessary. Chaudhry criticised what he described as inadequate resources for the KP Police, including lower salaries compared to those of police forces in other provinces. He also questioned the availability of protective equipment, armoured vehicles, security arrangements, forensic laboratories and residential facilities for police personnel. He questioned the proposed composition of a six-member body under the new law, saying it would comprise members of the provincial assembly. “Why not include opposition members, civil society representatives, journalists, police officers and judges? They could also provide valuable advice,” he said. Instead, he alleged, the provincial government had “brought in its own people” and sought to exercise control over the police down to the district and tehsil levels. Chaudhry said there could be differences between police forces in different provinces, such as changes in uniform colour or the creation of separate traffic police, but certain fundamental aspects had to remain uniform. He said it was “extremely unfortunate” that the proposed changes had been brought forward at a time when terrorism was at its peak in KP. Asked what options the federal government had, Chaudhry said the proposed law had only been approved by the provincial cabinet and would now be sent to the provincial assembly. He said there were several areas where federal laws continued to apply even after the 18th Amendment, adding that provinces could not legislate in a manner that conflicted with the Constitution or applicable federal laws and rules. “These are such rules that no province can change them,” he said, adding that the proposed legislation would likely be challenged before the courts. Chaudhry said that if the matter reached parliament and further legislation was required after debate, the federal government would not hesitate to take the matter forward. Responding to a question about the PTI’s call for a long march , the minister of state said all routes to the federal capital are open. However, he made it clear that the Islamabad High Court’s (IHC) decision would be implemented in letter and spirit to protect the lives and property of the people. KP governor vows to block proposed law if it reaches his office Meanwhile, Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi shared a video on X of his remarks at a conference, saying the provincial government wanted to turn the police into its “slave” and a “PTI tiger force”. “We will not allow the police to become anyone’s slave. They want the police to be subservient to them and become PTI’s tiger force. We will not allow the police to become tiger force. Instead, we will give the police the powers they need to take action against anyone who commits a wrongdoing,” he said. Kundi added that no government official, including the governor, chief minister or any other government functionary, could order the police to act unlawfully. “The law is equal for everyone,” he said, adding that the proposed law was facing criticism because of the PTI government’s record. Asked whether he would approve the proposed law if it came to him, Kundi said, “It has not even come to me yet, so why would I approve it? When this unconstitutional and illegal Police Act comes to me, I will not approve it.”

items.title: I Clinique du Littoral : le Fonds Islamique de Relance du FONSIS investit pour renforcer l’offre de soins sur la Petite Côte
items.description: À Ngaparou, la Clinique du Littoral accélère sa remise à niveau et prépare l’élargissement de son offre de soins. Soutenue par l’investissement du Fonds Islamique de Relance (FIR), filiale du Fonds Souverain d’Investissements Stratégiques (FONSIS), la clinique achève la rénovation de ses locaux et prépare l’installation de nouveaux équipements ainsi que l’ouverture de nouveaux services. Une relance tournée vers le renforcement des capacités de prise en charge et une offre de soins de proximité plus complète sur la Petite Côte. Créée en 2012 à Ngaparou, la Clinique du Littoral s’est progressivement développée autour d’une équipe de professionnels de santé, avec l’ambition de répondre aux besoins des populations de la Petite Côte. Au fil des années, l’établissement a étoffé ses activités, notamment dans le diagnostic et l’imagerie médicale. Cette trajectoire a été freinée par la pandémie de Covid-19 et ses répercussions sur l’activité de la clinique. La baisse de fréquentation et les difficultés financières qui ont suivi ont réduit ses capacités de renouvellement des équipements, entraînant l’interruption de plusieurs activités, dont celle du laboratoire en 2023. La clinique engage alors une démarche de relance, avec une priorité : remettre à niveau ses installations et retrouver les capacités nécessaires à son développement. Avec l’appui de l’ADEPME, elle entre en relation avec le Fonds Islamique de Relance. Filiale du FONSIS mise en place avec la Banque Islamique de Développement (BID), le FIR mobilise une enveloppe globale de 20 milliards de FCFA pour investir dans des PME et accompagner leur relance et leur développement, à travers des instruments conformes aux principes de la finance islamique. Après l’étude du projet et une visite de l’établissement, le FIR décide d’investir dans la Clinique du Littoral. Une remise à niveau qui prend forme L’investissement est consacré à la rénovation des locaux et à la modernisation progressive du plateau technique. Les travaux de rénovation et de mise à niveau sont aujourd’hui quasiment achevés. La prochaine étape porte sur l’installation d’une nouvelle radiologie numérique et d’un échographe 4D, ainsi que sur la remise à niveau du laboratoire. La clinique prépare parallèlement l’ouverture d’une maternité et d’un service de chirurgie, qui viendront élargir les possibilités de prise en charge à Ngaparou. « Sans le FIR, nous n’aurions pas pu arriver à ce niveau. Aujourd’hui, nous pouvons renforcer notre plateau technique et développer de nouveaux services pour nos patients », souligne Audrey Casahous, fondatrice de la Clinique du Littoral. Une offre de soins appelée à s’élargir La relance engagée ouvre de nouvelles perspectives pour la clinique et consolide une équipe composée à plus de 90 % de femmes. Elle accompagne aussi l’élargissement de l’offre de soins proposée aux populations de la Petite Côte. La maternité et la chirurgie viendront compléter les services proposés, tandis que la remise en activité du laboratoire et le renforcement de l’imagerie médicale élargiront les capacités de diagnostic et de prise en charge. La clinique projette, à terme, de compléter son plateau technique par de nouveaux équipements, notamment un scanner et une IRM. L’ancrage territorial de la clinique se traduit aussi par sa collaboration avec l’Hôpital de Mbour autour des besoins en produits sanguins. L’établissement hospitalier, qui dessert l’ensemble du département, dispose d’une capacité de stockage de 500 poches de sang, mais ses réserves disponibles se limitent souvent à une dizaine ou une quinzaine de poches. C’est dans ce contexte que la Clinique du Littoral organise, ce samedi 26 septembre, une journée de don de sang en partenariat avec l’Hôpital de Mbour. Au-delà de la collecte, l’initiative vise à encourager une pratique plus régulière du don, afin de contribuer à la constitution de réserves en amont des situations d’urgence et de réduire le recours aux dons de dernière minute. « Notre objectif est de mobiliser le maximum de donneurs au profit de l’Hôpital de Mbour », explique Audrey Casahous. La rénovation presque achevée marque ainsi une étape importante dans la relance de la Clinique du Littoral. Au-delà des nouveaux équipements et des services en préparation, l’enjeu est désormais de consolider l’activité de l’établissement, d’élargir les possibilités de prise en charge et de renforcer durablement l’offre de soins de proximité sur la Petite Côte.

items.title: Atiku’s lobbyist, Fani-Kayode trade $36m, $100m lawsuits
items.description: ABUJA — The legal dispute between former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s United States-based lobbyist, Karl Von Batten, and Nigeria’s Ambassador to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has escalated, with both sides threatening multimillion-dollar lawsuits in the United States. Von Batten-Montague-York, L.C., the lobbying firm engaged by Atiku, said it had been cleared to proceed with a $36 million federal lawsuit against Fani-Kayode and President Bola Tinubu over alleged threats to kidnap and physically harm Von Batten. The firm said in a statement on Wednesday that the suit would be filed next week before the United States District Court for the District of Columbia. According to the firm, the proposed action arose from what it described as threats allegedly made by Fani-Kayode against Von Batten, which it further claimed were connected to an organised criminal conspiracy involving the Nigerian Presidency. The firm also said it would contact United States, United Kingdom and European Union immigration authorities after filing the suit to seek a review of Fani-Kayode’s travel or visa status in connection with the allegations. The proposed litigation is the latest development in an escalating dispute between Von Batten and Fani-Kayode over allegations concerning Tinubu. In recent weeks, Von Batten’s firm has sought the release of United States government records relating to Tinubu’s past dealings with US drug-enforcement authorities, including through Freedom of Information Act requests and related litigation. The firm said in July that it had begun providing records concerning allegations against Tinubu to officials of the US Department of Justice, members of the Donald Trump administration, Congress and senior congressional staff. Fani-Kayode challenges him Fani-Kayode has challenged Von Batten to substantiate his allegations and has denied threatening to kidnap or physically harm him. In a statement responding to the planned $36 million suit, Fani-Kayode said he was not interested in harming or kidnapping Von Batten and insisted that he had acted within the law. He also said he would challenge Von Batten’s allegations through legal means. Fani-Kayode subsequently announced plans to institute a $100 million lawsuit against Von Batten, alleging libel and defamation. He said his lawyers would seek damages of at least $100 million in a US court over what he described as false and damaging allegations against him. The ambassador also said he would seek Von Batten’s extradition to Nigeria to face proceedings over alleged violations of Nigerian cybercrime and criminal-defamation laws. Fani-Kayode challenged the lobbyist to make public any evidence supporting his allegation that he, Tinubu or the Federal Government had threatened him. He further rejected allegations that the Nigerian government engages in kidnapping, physical harm or state-sponsored violence against political opponents or critics. The latest exchange follows a series of statements and social media posts by both sides, with Von Batten continuing his campaign concerning US records linked to allegations against Tinubu, while Fani-Kayode has repeatedly disputed the claims and questioned the lobbyist’s assertions. As of Thursday, the proposed $36 million action had not been confirmed as filed in the US federal court. The allegations made by the lobbying firm against Tinubu and Fani-Kayode, as well as Fani-Kayode’s counter-allegations against Von Batten, remain disputed and have not been established by a court. The post Atiku’s lobbyist, Fani-Kayode trade $36m, $100m lawsuits appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: UNGA: ‘Tinubu hiding to avoid arrest by Trump’ — Atiku’s campaign
items.description: Kenneth Okonkwo, spokesperson for the Atiku Abubakar Presidential Campaign, has alleged that President Bola Tinubu is avoiding the United States because he fears possible arrest by US President Donald Trump. Okonkwo made the claim while reacting to Tinubu’s absence from the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York on an appearance on Arise New’s Prime Time programme, where Vice President Kashim Shettima is representing Nigeria. Okonkwo questioned why Tinubu had again stayed away from the annual gathering, alleging that the president was deliberately avoiding the United States because of renewed attention to past drug-related allegations and legal records involving him. “Tinubu is hiding. He is running away from being arrested by Trump,” Okonkwo alleged. He also said Tinubu’s continued absence from the UNGA was difficult to explain, noting that the president had not personally attended the gathering for three consecutive years after attending the 2023 session. “What is he doing? He has not been to the United Nations for three consecutive years. A reasonable man should say that he is hiding from the United States of America,” Okonkwo said. The former Labour Party chieftain also referred to earlier comments attributed to Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, who had said Tinubu would attend the UNGA and sit in the front row with Trump. “Remember, the ambassador to the United Nations, Jimoh Ibrahim, had told us gleefully that the president was going to come and sit in the front row with President Trump to represent us. What happened? Lies. The President did not go,” he said. Okonkwo linked Tinubu’s absence to renewed discussions over historical US records concerning the president, including a civil forfeiture matter involving about $460,000 in 1993. “Now, how come there is a paper filed by your president that he does not want his file to be released in the United States of America? That is allegedly for his involvement in alleged drug dealing,” he said. The current legal dispute concerns access to US government records under the Freedom of Information Act. The Presidency has maintained that the matter is a civil records disclosure dispute and not a criminal case against Tinubu. “For clarity, the matter is a civil records disclosure dispute under the United States Freedom of Information Act. It is not a criminal case against President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, nor has the court found him guilty of any criminal wrongdoing,” Presidential spokesman Bayo Onanuga said. There have also been earlier claims that Tinubu could face arrest if he travelled to the US for the UNGA. However, Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Jimoh Ibrahim, said in September that the Nigerian Mission in New York had received no communication from the US government indicating any restriction on Tinubu’s movement. Ibrahim also said representatives of member states attending official UN activities enjoy protections under the 1947 UN US Headquarters Agreement. The Presidency has meanwhile said Tinubu’s absence from the UNGA is because he is on an extended working vacation and has continued to direct affairs of government from abroad. The State House said Tinubu departed Nigeria on August 30 and later travelled to Paris, where he held meetings with French President Emmanuel Macron and other officials. It said he had delegated Shettima to represent him at the UNGA. Tinubu attended the 78th UNGA in 2023, while Shettima represented him at the 2024 and 2025 sessions. Okonkwo, however, maintained that the President’s repeated absence raises questions about his decision to stay away from the United States. “Every reasonable man will say he is running away from the United States of America,” he said. items.title: AI must not become 'another facet of ongoing arms race', Pakistan tells UNSC
items.description: Pakistan has stressed the need to prevent artificial intelligence (AI) from becoming “another facet of the ongoing arms race”, as the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) was briefed by leaders of major AI firms. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar delivered Pakistan’s statement at the meeting of the top UN body, where AI executives said the technology calls for heightened vigilance. Speaking at the France-chaired briefing on artificial intelligence and international security, DPM Dar said: “We must ensure that AI does not become another facet of the ongoing arms race. “Concerted efforts are required to erect the necessary guardrails, regulations and governance frameworks. In the military domain, we need measures of restraint and confidence-building to address the risks of miscalculation and compressed decision-making.” OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue and Yoshua Bengio, co-chair of the UN International Independent Panel on AI, also briefed the council. Anthropic’s CEO pledged to slow down where needed to ensure the safety of new releases, while Altman also said that “this moment calls for extreme care”. In his remarks, shared by the Foreign Office (FO) on Thursday, DPM Dar emphasised that the “foremost priority is to retain human judgement and control in all stages of AI design, development, and integration”. He said humans must remain in control to define structures of AI systems as well as to limit the speed and nature of future capabilities. The deputy premier further said that the technology should not be a “monopoly of a few actors”, calling for international collaboration in AI development. He noted that AI was “supercharging existing challenges such as misinformation, fake news, cyber attacks, including on critical infrastructure by state and non-state actors”. “We must undertake concrete action to address the gaps and challenges that carry huge implications for peace and security,” he maintained. “Pakistan takes the call to pace the AI frontier seriously,” the DPM told the UNSC. “We welcome the recognition that no single company or country can manage these risks alone, and that competitive pressures are driving a race that no one can win safely,” he observed. At the same time, Dar cautioned that efforts to pace the AI frontier “must not become a new form of gatekeeping” and measures pursued in the name of safety “must not become instruments of denial of technology”. He emphasised that decisions on how to manage AI risks “cannot rest with a handful of companies or capitals”. “Therefore, it is critical to avoid fragmentation in AI development and governance. Discriminatory agendas and inequitable forums with select representation are not helpful,” he asserted. The deputy premier called for AI governance to be taken up in “representative and inclusive forums with universal participation under UN auspices”. The minister welcomed the first UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance in Geneva and highlighted Pakistan’s founding membership of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organisation (WAICO), terming the latter a “concrete step towards promoting the development of AI for good and for all”. The meeting was also attended by foreign ministers of Denmark and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the UK foreign secretary, and the director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, according to FO. Senior representatives from Panama, Greece, Somalia, Bahrain, Latvia, Colombia, China, Russia and Liberia also participated. France’s Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot urged joint action within the UN framework and with companies to set rules for a new era. But diplomatic efforts could clash with the United States’ position. Michael Kratsios, director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, said rapid advancement is not a reason to pause AI’s development or constrain it with new governance structures. Tech chiefs urge caution in AI development The UNSC meeting followed weeks of global headlines about the risks of uncontrollable AI and calls for a slowdown, which have been resisted by US President Donald Trump. “The industry must not accept too much technological risk just because the benefits are too great and important to slow down,” the OpenAI CEO told the United Nations’ top body. He warned that as AI systems become more capable and autonomous, they could move faster than institutions or concentrate power into too few hands. Altman also urged governments to work with each other and the industry on decisions shaping the technology’s future. “In our history, there have been times where countries who compete and don’t always like each other very much still come together for shared interests and the collective good in the face of a powerful new technology,” he said. “We believe this must be one of those times,” he added. Altman said his company would try to walk a “middle path”. “We don’t want to fall into the trap of blind optimism,” he said, but cautioned against falling into “doomerism” too. Speaking after Altman, the Anthropic CEO said his company understands that as AI models become more powerful, “even more stringent standards of safety will be required”. He said Anthropic aims to improve its ability to prevent misuse of the technology. “We will slow down as much as necessary in order to make sure that every successive AI technology that we release is actually safe,” Amodei said in a video feed. “If managed poorly, I even believe that AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole,” he added. Delangue of Hugging Face noted that while his company was targeted by AI, it also used the technology to fend off the attacks. “The world needs open-source AI more than ever to defend itself.”

items.title: Four suspected Boko Haram terrorists arrested in Yobe
items.description: By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman, Damaturu Troops of the Joint Task Force, North East, Operation Hadin Kai, have arrested four suspected Boko Haram terrorists following a night ambush in Gujba Local Government Area of Yobe State. The arrests were made during sustained operations conducted between September 15 and 22, 2026, which also resulted in the surrender of 11 suspected terrorists and the arrest of nine suspected drug dealers. The Acting Military Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force North East, Operation Hadin Kai, Captain Mohammed Goni, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday. According to him, troops of 27 Task Force Brigade, working with members of the Civilian Joint Task Force, laid an ambush east of Azare village in Gujba at about 11pm on September 21. He said the troops engaged suspected terrorists in a firefight, forcing some of them to flee, while four were subsequently arrested during an exploitation of the area. The military said blood traces found around the scene indicated that some of the fleeing suspects might have sustained injuries during the encounter. Recovered items included four bicycles, groceries, one sheep and expended 7.62mm special ammunition cases. The military said the suspects and recovered items had been taken into custody for further investigation, while troops continued to exploit the area. In a separate operation, troops of the brigade also arrested nine suspected drug dealers during a routine patrol in Buni Yadi, Gujba LGA, on September 19. The suspects were allegedly found with suspected illicit drugs and cannabis, two mobile phones and N85,900 cash. The military said the suspects and exhibits were handed over to the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency for further investigation and possible prosecution. It added that the cumulative operational successes during the period also included the recovery of a vehicle, ammunition and other logistics items. The military said the operations were aimed at disrupting terrorist and criminal networks and denying them freedom of action across the Joint Operations Area. The post Four suspected Boko Haram terrorists arrested in Yobe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Energie : l’Afrique centrale dessine sa politique à l’horizon 2035 à Bujumbura
items.description: © DR Bujumbura accueille du 23 au 25 septembre 2026 l'atelier régional d'examen et de validation du rapport sur l'état des lieux du secteur énergétique de l'Afrique centrale. Experts des États membres de la CEEAC et partenaires techniques planchent sur le diagnostic et les perspectives pour doter la sous-région d'une Politique Énergétique Commune. Cap sur 2035 pour l'énergie en Afrique centrale. Bujumbura (République du Burundi) accueille du 23 au 25 septembre 2026, l'atelier régional d'examen et de validation du rapport sur la situation actuelle et les perspectives du secteur énergétique à l'horizon 2035. Trois jours durant, les experts de la quasi-totalité des Etats membres de la CEEAC et partenaires techniques feront un état des lieux des défis qui minent le développement du secteur. L'objectif : passer du diagnostic à l'adoption d'une Politique Énergétique de la Communauté. Les participants analyseront les cadres politique, institutionnel, juridique et financier, la gouvernance, le potentiel en énergies primaires et le niveau de valorisation, ainsi que l'état des infrastructures régionales (hydrocarbures, hydroélectricité, renouvelables, biomasse). En prélude, la délégation de la Commission CEEAC conduite par le Directeur de l'énergie, Désiré Armand Ndemazagoa Backotta, a été reçue par le Chef du Bureau de liaison au Burundi, Marcelino Nko Ruku, par le ministre burundais Dr Hassan Kibeya et par la représentante de la BAD, Diawara Muna. Au cœur des échanges : accès universel à l'électricité, interconnexions électriques et renforcement de la coopération. La CEEAC soutient déjà l'intégration énergétique via le PEAC, le CEREEAC et la CORREAC pour harmoniser les réglementations et promouvoir les investissements. Cet article Energie : l'Afrique centrale dessine sa politique à l'horizon 2035 à Bujumbura est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

Validé le 23 septembre 2026 au Ministère de la Défense à Yaoundé, ce document financé par le DHAPP américain vise à renforcer la riposte au sein des forces de défense pour la période allant du 1er octobre 2026 au 30 septembre 2027. La riposte se structure dans les rangs. Le secteur interarmées dispose désormais de son micro-plan d'action VIH pour la période 2026-2027. Le document a été validé le mercredi 23 septembre 2026, au cours d'une réunion tenue dans la salle de conférence du Ministère de la Défense (MINDEF), à Yaoundé. Financé par le Department of Defense HIV/AIDS Prevention Program (DHAPP), ce micro-plan vise à renforcer et à structurer les interventions de lutte contre le VIH au sein du secteur interarmées. Sa mise en œuvre, prévue du 1er octobre 2026 au 30 septembre 2027, sera assurée par HEADA, avec l'appui du financement DHAPP. Au terme des échanges, les différentes instances participantes ont validé le document, tout en formulant une recommandation majeure : mettre le micro-plan en conformité avec le canevas de planification du CNLS, afin d'assurer son harmonisation avec les outils nationaux de planification de la riposte au VIH. Le document finalisé devra être transmis au CNLS avant la fin du mois de septembre 2026, en vue de poursuivre le processus de coordination et de préparer la mise en œuvre des activités prévues sur le terrain. Cet article Lutte contre le VIH : le Secteur Interarmées valide son micro-plan d'action 2026-2027 est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Bagbin recalls Parliament for September 29 sitting following calls to probe narcotics seizures
items.description: Speaker of Parliament, Rt. Hon. Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin, has summoned Parliament to sit on Tuesday, September 29, 2026, in accordance with Article 112(3) of the 1992 Constitution and Order 53 of the Standing Orders of Parliament. A notice issued by the Office of the Speaker on Thursday, September 24, states that the House will convene at 12 noon at Parliament House in Accra. The notice does not state the specific reason for the recall. “Pursuant to Article 112(3) of the Constitution and Order 53 of the Standing Orders of the Parliament, I, Rt. Hon. Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin, the Speaker of Parliament, hereby summon Parliament to sit on Tuesday, 29th September, 2026 at twelve noon at Parliament House, Accra,” the notice said. However, the recall comes amid growing concerns over a series of major narcotics seizures linked to consignments from Ghana. Screenshot The Minority in Parliament has petitioned the Speaker for an extraordinary sitting, citing what it says are urgent national security concerns and calling for scrutiny of Ghana’s ports, customs controls, intelligence gathering and narcotics enforcement systems. The Minority has cited several seizures since 2025 which it says have a combined value of more than US$1 billion. Among them are the seizure of more than 3.3 tonnes of cocaine at Pedu Junction in March 2025 and the recent interception of nearly 3.9 tonnes of cocaine at the Port of Dunkirk in France from a container that had departed Ghana. The caucus wants Parliament to examine how the consignments were processed, inspected and cleared, as well as the roles of the relevant security and state agencies. It has also called for responsible Ministers and officials from institutions including the Narcotics Control Commission, Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority, Ghana Revenue Authority and National Intelligence Bureau to appear before the House. The planned sitting comes after differing views within Parliament over whether a recall is necessary. While the Minority has argued that the scale of the seizures warrants urgent parliamentary oversight, some Majority MPs have questioned the need for a full recall while investigations by the relevant agencies remain ongoing. The notice was dated September 24, 2026, and signed by Speaker Alban Bagbin. Parliament’s official website currently lists the House as being on recess and shows an emergency meeting on its parliamentary calendar.

items.title: Average lending rate stood at 15.9% as of August 2026
items.description: Ghana’s average lending rate stood at 15.9% as of the end of August 2026, according to data from the Bank of Ghana. The average cost of loans has been hovering around 15% since May 2026. This means one would pay about 1.31% per month on every loan, excluding other fees and charges. Similarly, the Ghana Reference Rate also stood at 10.61% in August 2026, from 10.59% in July 2026. According to the Bank of Ghana’s September 2026 Summary of Economic and Financial Data, the average lending rate stood at 20.58% in January 2026, but fell to 19.17% in February 2026 and subsequently to 17.74% in March 2026. It again fell to 16.33% in April 2026. It hovered around 15.83%, 15.64% and 15.80% in May 2026, June 2026 and July 2026 respectively. In July 2026, the Bank of Ghana held its policy rate unchanged at 14%, citing risks to inflation and external pressure from the Middle East war that had pushed oil prices very high. Average Lending Rates Vary Among Banks The average lending rates, however, vary among banks, the sectors they lend to, and borrowers. Some banks offer loans equivalent to the Ghana Reference Rate, whilst others will charge rates as high as 30% per annum. Presently, some banks are offering structured loans to employees at about 12% on the average.

items.title: NDLEA busts Nigerian-Mexican meth cartel, arraigns 2 in Enugu
items.description: … Court fixes Oct. 21 for trial By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, NDLEA, has dismantled a Nigerian-Mexican drug cartel operating a clandestine methamphetamine laboratory in Eziama community, Obeagu, Awgu Local Government Area of Enugu State. The agency also arrested and arraigned two suspected kingpins, 45-year-old Chukwu Christopher, alias Brown, and 60-year-old Chukwu Monday, alias George, over their alleged involvement in the operation. The suspects were allegedly working with Rodriguez Villanueva, a suspected member of a Mexican drug cartel based in Mexico City, following months of intelligence gathering and surveillance by the NDLEA. Christopher and Monday were arraigned before Justice Mabel Taiye Segun-Bello of the Federal High Court, Enugu Judicial Division, on a five-count charge bordering on conspiracy, organisation, management and financing of a drug trafficking organisation and unlawful possession of precursor chemicals allegedly used in methamphetamine production. The charges were brought under the NDLEA Act. Following their pleas, the court fixed October 21, 2026, for trial after the agency applied for an accelerated hearing. Also named in the charge but currently at large are Uchenna, alias Uche; Celestine Ikemefuna Iwuchukwu; and Villanueva. According to the NDLEA, investigations by its Special Operations Unit uncovered a sophisticated transnational operation involving the Nigerian and Mexican suspects. The agency said surveillance conducted between December 1 and 4, 2025, tracked Christopher’s movements across Lagos, Enugu and Anambra states before operatives traced him to a compound in Obeagu. A search of the premises allegedly led to the discovery of a clandestine laboratory equipped with improvised reactors and distillation equipment and capable of producing methamphetamine in commercial quantities. The NDLEA said the facility was similar to other clandestine laboratories recently dismantled in Ogun, Oyo and Ebonyi states. Recovered from the premises, according to the agency, were 690 litres of methylamine, 1,000 litres of isopropyl alcohol, 300 litres of hydrochloric acid, 290 litres each of toluene and acetone, 400 litres of liquid sodium hydroxide, 125kg of N-phenylacetamide, 414kg of lead acetate and 769.6kg of tartaric acid, among other controlled substances. The agency said the quantity and combination of chemicals were consistent with a P2P-based methamphetamine manufacturing operation. A related search of Monday’s family residence allegedly yielded eight large fuel tanks, four commercial gas burners, four dehydrators and 11kg of ephedrine. Reacting to the development, NDLEA Chairman/Chief Executive, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), reaffirmed the agency’s determination to track down all suspects linked to the alleged cartel. Marwa commended the officers involved in the operation for what he described as their professionalism and commitment in dismantling the international drug syndicate. He said the Enugu operation demonstrated that Nigeria would not be allowed to become a haven for transnational drug cartels. Marwa added that the agency would continue to rely on intelligence-driven operations and international partnerships to disrupt illicit drug production and trafficking. He also directed NDLEA personnel to sustain enforcement operations until the country is rid of illicit drug production and trafficking. The post NDLEA busts Nigerian-Mexican meth cartel, arraigns 2 in Enugu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Cameroun/ Tiko : cinq morts après le chavirement d’une pirogue de pèlerins à Mudeka
items.description: © Voa Afrique Au moins cinq personnes sont mortes et plusieurs autres blessées dans la nuit du 22 au 23 septembre 2026 après le chavirement d'une embarcation transportant des chrétiens en pèlerinage à Mudeka, arrondissement de Tiko. La nuit du pèlerinage a viré au drame. Une embarcation transportant des chrétiens en pèlerinage a chaviré au large de Mudeka, dans l'arrondissement de Tiko, département du Fako, Région du Sud-Ouest. Le bilan fait état de cinq morts. Un bilan confirmé par le préfet du département du Fako, Viang Mekala, dans un communiqué cité par la Crtv au cours des éditions de journaux ce jeudi matin. Les victimes, quatre filles et un garçon, étaient, selon les premières informations, des jeunes inscrits dans des établissements scolaires de Buea qui se rendaient sur une île de la zone dans le cadre de ce pèlerinage. Les circonstances exactes du chavirement restent encore floues et font l'objet d'une enquête ouverte par les autorités. Les rescapés, blessés, ont été évacués et reçoivent des soins à l'hôpital baptiste Mbingo de Mutengene. Les corps des cinq victimes quant à eux ont été transférés à la morgue de l'hôpital de district de Tiko. Une deuxième tragédie en mer en 17 jours Ce drame survient quelques semaines après un autre accident mortel en mer dans le Sud-Ouest. Le 6 septembre 2026, huit personnes avaient trouvé la mort dans la collision de deux embarcations à Kombo Itindi, dans le département du Ndian. Deux drames qui relancent la question cruciale de la sécurité de la navigation artisanale sur la côte camerounaise, particulièrement pendant la saison des pluies, avec des pirogues souvent surchargées et sans gilets de sauvetage. Cet article Cameroun/ Tiko : cinq morts après le chavirement d'une pirogue de pèlerins à Mudeka est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Old Niger Bridge: First rehabilitated phase to reopen next week — Umahi
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — The Minister of Works, Engr. David Umahi, has announced that the first phase of the rehabilitation of the old Niger Bridge linking Anambra and Delta states will reopen to traffic next week. Umahi made the announcement during an inspection of the ongoing rehabilitation works on the bridge, which was closed to traffic after sections were vandalised, prompting the diversion of traffic to the Second Niger Bridge. The contract for the rehabilitation was awarded on September 7, 2026. The minister said the bolts and expansion joints removed by vandals had been replaced, while resurfacing of the bridge with asphalt and concrete was ongoing. He said he would return next week to open the completed first phase to traffic, while other rehabilitation works would continue. Umahi directed that the kerbs along the bridge be painted with oil paint and that the metal components of the bridge up to a specified height also be repainted. He ordered the immediate removal of all illegal advertisements on the bridge, warning that anyone seeking to advertise there must obtain approval from the Federal Ministry of Works. The minister also directed that roadblocks, task forces and tax collection points located within 200 metres of the bridge be removed, saying they posed safety risks by creating traffic congestion. “There shall no longer be road blocks or task force or tax people 200 meters from the bridge because it is creating a dangerous situation. Bridges are not built for static checkpoints,” he said. Umahi directed that the order be communicated to the governors of Anambra and Delta states, as well as heads of security agencies. He also ordered the installation of additional solar lights and directed that the existing closed-circuit television cameras on the bridge be linked immediately to the Second Niger Bridge. The minister said he had constituted a committee to conduct an empirical assessment of the condition of the bridge above and below the water level. “I have also set up a committee to do empirical evaluation of what is happening below and above the water level under the bridge,” he said, adding that the committee would submit its report before the end of the work on Thursday. Umahi stressed the need for collective protection of public infrastructure, noting that the country was losing significant resources to vandalism. Umahi canvasses support for Tinubu The minister commended President Bola Tinubu for what he described as prompt intervention in infrastructure development across the country. He said the South-East and South-South regions should support the President because of ongoing infrastructure projects in the areas. Umahi specifically urged voters in the regions to support Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election, while challenging other presidential aspirants to account for their contributions to infrastructure development in the South-East. “The South East and South South must support the President because of the massive infrastructure development that is ongoing in the two zones,” he said. He also referred to former Anambra State governor and presidential candidate Peter Obi, saying the minister regarded him as a brother but urging voters to support Tinubu. “We are not calling out anybody because we want to insult him. Peter Obi is our brother, but we should be strategic and wise and support President Bola Tinubu,” Umahi said. He said although voters in the South-East did not support Tinubu sufficiently in the 2023 election, his administration had embarked on infrastructure projects in the region. He also urged presidential aides from the South-East and South-South to beautify the Niger Bridge and decorate it with images of Tinubu as a way of appreciating the President’s intervention in infrastructure development. items.title: Sénégal-Mozambique : Pape Gueye capitaine, Koulibaly attendu sur le banc ?
items.description: Pour ses premiers pas à la tête de l’équipe nationale du Sénégal, Patrick Vieira s’apprête à apporter quelques ajustements à la configuration habituelle de la Tanière. Face au Mozambique, vendredi à 13 heures heure de Dakar, dans le cadre des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027, plusieurs changements pourraient être observés, notamment au niveau du leadership. Kalidou Koulibaly, figure incontournable de la sélection depuis de nombreuses années, ne devrait pas être aligné d’entrée. Le défenseur d’Al-Hilal pourrait ainsi débuter la rencontre sur le banc, dans une volonté du nouveau sélectionneur de faire évoluer progressivement certains repères au sein du groupe. Cette décision ne remettrait pas en cause la place du défenseur dans la Tanière. Son expérience et son vécu international devraient plutôt être mis au service de la nouvelle génération, alors que Vieira entend installer progressivement ses propres équilibres et une nouvelle dynamique collective. Iliman et Sarr suspendus Le brassard devrait, lui, revenir à Pape Gueye. Le milieu de Villarreal est appelé à assumer cette responsabilité à l’occasion de cette première rencontre de l’ère Vieira. Son retour en sélection, après avoir un temps envisagé de mettre un terme à son aventure internationale, prend ainsi une dimension particulière. Le choix de Pape Gueye s’explique également par les absences d’Ismaïla Sarr et d’Iliman Ndiaye, tous deux suspendus pour cette affiche. En leur absence, le milieu de terrain pourrait donc conduire les Lions sur le terrain face aux Mambas. Au-delà du résultat attendu dans ces éliminatoires, cette rencontre permettra surtout de mesurer les premiers contours du projet de Patrick Vieira. Avec une hiérarchie appelée à évoluer et des responsabilités redistribuées, le nouveau sélectionneur semble vouloir imprimer progressivement sa marque à la Tanière. C.G. DIOP

items.title: 2027: Lagos APC dismisses Rhodes-Vivour, Gbadamosi ticket as ‘Political Experiment’
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress, APC, has described the newly unveiled governorship ticket of Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour and Babatunde Gbadamosi under the African Democratic Congress, ADC, as a “political experiment” ahead of the 2027 election. In a statement on Thursday, Lagos APC Publicity Secretary, Seye Oladejo, said the emergence of the opposition candidates did not automatically translate into governing experience or grassroots political structure. Oladejo argued that Lagos was not an “internship centre” for political experimentation, stressing that governing the state required experience in managing its bureaucracy, budget and complex infrastructure. He also questioned the executive experience of the two candidates, citing their participation in different political parties in previous election cycles. According to him, Rhodes-Vivour previously contested under the KOWA Party, Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, and Labour Party, before emerging as the ADC candidate, while Gbadamosi had contested under the Abundant Nigeria Renewal Party, ANRP/Action Democratic Party, ADP, and PDP. “There is absolutely nothing wrong with political evolution, but party-hopping is not political institution-building. “Lagos is a sophisticated economy with complex infrastructure and demanding urban-management challenges. Where is the record of managing a state bureaucracy or supervising a state budget?” Oladejo asked. The APC spokesman acknowledged that Rhodes-Vivour finished second in the 2023 governorship election, scoring 312,329 votes against Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu’s 762,134 votes. He, however, argued that electoral performance should not be equated with administrative capacity. Oladejo challenged the ADC candidates to present a clear plan for governing Lagos beyond their social media presence, including details of project financing, implementation and continuity of ongoing government projects. “The Lagos APC welcomes the Rhodes-Vivour/Gbadamosi ticket — let the contest begin. “However, the opposition should not expect Lagosians to confuse political noise with political strength, or electoral ambition with governing capacity,” he said. items.title: LAWMA arrests 7 over illegal dumping on Lagos Island
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — The Lagos Waste Management Authority, LAWMA, has arrested seven suspected illegal waste dumpers during an overnight enforcement operation in the Pattey area of Lagos Island. The operation, conducted on Wednesday, was part of the agency’s ongoing efforts to eliminate illegal waste disposal black spots and enforce environmental regulations across the state. The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of LAWMA, Dr Muyiwa Gbadegesin, said the suspects were apprehended for prosecution. The suspects were identified as Nafisat Alabi, 30, from Kwara State; Aminullah Abdulrasheed, 49, Kwara; Segun Adeyemi, 45, Ogun; Gboyega Osuntuyi, 44, Ekiti; Segun Olowe, 26, Osun; Adebayo Ibrahim, 29, Oyo; and Stephen Ogboru, 36, Delta. The enforcement operation, however, encountered resistance when a group of suspected hoodlums reportedly stormed the LAWMA field office in the area and attempted to interfere with the officers. The situation was brought under control after the Area Commander of the Lion Building Police Station deployed a tactical team to support the enforcement personnel. Gbadegesin said LAWMA would continue to enforce waste management regulations across the state. “LAWMA will not relent in enforcing waste management regulations. Sustained monitoring and enforcement remain essential to curbing illegal dumping and promoting responsible waste practices,” he said. The seven suspects have been transferred to the Task Force Office in Oshodi for prosecution. Gbadegesin commended the police for their prompt intervention and urged residents, traders and local businesses to support LAWMA’s efforts. He also warned against obstructing enforcement personnel carrying out their duties. The post LAWMA arrests 7 over illegal dumping on Lagos Island appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ActionAid to FG: Keep King’s College public, reject concession
items.description: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA — Following the controversy surrounding the proposed concession of King’s College, Lagos, ActionAid Nigeria, AAN, has called on the Federal Government to retain the school as a public institution. Speaking with Vanguard, Country Director of AAN, Dr Andrew Mamedu, said the organisation was concerned about the controversy, particularly against the backdrop of Nigeria’s education crisis. Mamedu said public education must remain public in purpose and not merely in name. “Many of today’s leaders benefited from free or heavily subsidised education. We cannot benefit from that ladder and then pull it away from the children coming behind us,” he said. He noted that the Federal Government had earlier estimated that about 15 million Nigerian children were out of school, arguing that government’s priority should be expanding affordable public education rather than creating uncertainty over access. “When millions of children are already outside the classroom because of poverty, insecurity and other barriers, our priority should be expanding affordable public education, not creating uncertainty around access to it,” he said. Mamedu acknowledged the Federal Government’s explanation that King’s College had not been sold, that government would retain ownership and that there was currently no plan to extend the arrangement to other Federal Unity Colleges. He, however, said the concern went beyond ownership. “The real question is whether public education will remain affordable, accessible and genuinely public in purpose,” he said. According to him, education, healthcare, water and other essential social services are rights and should not be structured in ways that could price poor and vulnerable Nigerians out. “Education is one of the strongest pathways out of poverty. If quality public education becomes increasingly dependent on private financing and management, children from low-income families may be the first to lose access,” he said. The AAN director also expressed concern over reports that some parents had kept their children away from school in protest, warning that children should not bear the consequences of disagreements between government and stakeholders. He urged the Federal Government to use the ongoing review to engage parents, workers and other stakeholders transparently. Mamedu also called for the agreement to be made public, with clear provisions on future fees and guarantees of access for children from poor families. Meanwhile, staff of Federal Unity Colleges across the country reportedly defied the Federal Government’s directive to resume academic activities on Monday, sustaining their indefinite strike over the proposed concession of King’s College, Lagos. Parents also kept their children away from the schools as the industrial action continued. The post ActionAid to FG: Keep King’s College public, reject concession appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le Game Art Park, un espace de loisirs inclusif à Gammarth
items.description: Le Game Art Park est un parc de loisirs situé à Gammarth, dans la banlieue nord de Tunis, conçu pour conjuguer inclusion sociale, accessibilité et durabilité environnementale. Ce complexe d’environ 10 000 mètres carrés réalisé avec le soutien de la Coopération italienne constitue, selon l’Agence italienne pour la coopération au développement (AICS), le premier parc de loisirs écologique de Tunisie et le premier complexe inclusif de ce type en Afrique. Le projet, porté par l’entrepreneur tunisien Mourad Chabchoub via la société Deals BM, vise à rendre les activités de loisirs accessibles aux personnes à mobilité réduite. Les parcours, les infrastructures et les activités ont été conçus dès le départ pour permettre une utilisation sans barrières, indique l’AICS dans un article signé par Sarah Corti, experte en communication, et Anis Khelifi, chef de programme (secteur privé) à l’AICS Tunis. Le parc comprend des aires de jeux, un amphithéâtre en plein air de 400 places, un labyrinthe végétal, des dômes écologiques destinés à des activités éducatives pour les enfants, des parcours de santé et des espaces de restauration. Le développement d’activités sportives paralympiques est également prévu, avec une salle de sport polyvalente, une piscine-lagon à entrée progressive dans l’eau et un espace dédié aux personnes atteintes de troubles du spectre autistique. Les matériaux utilisés pour la structure sont en grande partie naturels ou recyclés. Au sein du complexe a également été développé Rest’Art, un concept alliant restauration et spectacle, visant à offrir aux humoristes et aux jeunes artistes un espace professionnel ainsi qu’une source de revenus stable. Les promoteurs du projet Game Art Park souhaitent ainsi adopter un modèle d’ «entreprise sociale» , en conciliant viabilité économique et objectifs sociaux. L’investissement total pour le projet s’élève à 2,115 millions de dinars tunisiens. Une partie de l’opération a été financée par un prêt de 200 000 dinars, accordé par la Banque de Tunisie et des Émirats (BTE) pour une durée de sept ans, incluant deux années de différé d’amortissement. Ce financement, débloqué en 2024 pour les travaux d’aménagement, s’inscrit dans le volet dédié à l’économie sociale et solidaire du Programme de soutien au secteur privé et à l’inclusion financière (Prasoc) de la Coopération italienne. Actuellement, Game Art Park emploie sept personnes en contrat à durée indéterminée, tandis que le plan de développement prévoit d’atteindre, à moyen terme, un effectif de 35 à 40 emplois directs. Selon l’AICS, le Prasoc, programme dédié à l'accessibilité et à l'entrepreneuriat social, a financé près de 400 opérations en Tunisie, contribuant à la création ou à la consolidation de plus de 4 000 emplois. L’initiative de Gammarth, souligne l’Agence, s’inscrit dans la stratégie de la Coopération italienne visant à faciliter l’accès au crédit pour les entreprises tunisiennes et à soutenir des modèles économiques capables d’associer emploi, inclusion sociale et durabilité environnementale. D’après Ansa . Game Art Park à Gammarth | Un espace animé pour toute la famille L’article Le Game Art Park, un espace de loisirs inclusif à Gammarth est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Punjab police FIRs leave LHC chief justice worried about judges ‘losing eyesight’
items.description: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Thursday directed the Punjab police to increase the font size used in first information reports (FIRs) across the province. Chief Justice Aalia Neelum issued the direction during a hearing on an issue arising from a contempt of court petition. Inspector General of Police (IGP) Rao Abdul Kareem appeared before the court on its orders. The chief justice expressed displeasure over FIRs being printed in small fonts, observing that the documents were difficult to read. She remarked that the problem was being seen in case after case. “While police are saving paper, we are losing our eyesight,” the chief justice remarked. She observed that fitting the narration of three pages onto a single page would obviously make the font unreadable. The CJ directed the IGP to ensure that FIRs across Punjab were printed in a uniform, larger font. The IGP told the court that a letter had already been sent to the chairman of the Punjab Information Technology Board regarding an increase in the font size. The CJ sought a detailed report from the IGP on the steps taken in this regard and adjourned the hearing until Sept 29. She also sought a separate report on a contempt of court petition filed by a citizen against the police. On Wednesday, during hearing of a petition filed by a citizen, Superintendent of Police (SP) Abdullah appeared before the court on behalf of the Chung police. When Justice Neelum asked SP Abdullah to read the FIR aloud, he was unable to properly read or narrate its contents. “Why is the FIR not readable? I cannot understand what has been written in it,” the chief justice remarked. She also took a sarcastic jab at the handwriting, observing that it looked like “flies” and quipping: “Even the size of the flies is bigger [than this].”

items.title: Repeated cocaine seizures could hurt Ghana’s trade reputation – CDM
items.description: The Centre for Democratic Movement (CDM) has warned that the growing number of international narcotics seizures involving consignments linked to Ghana could have consequences for the country’s reputation, legitimate exporters and citizens travelling or doing business abroad. The organisation said the recent Dunkirk seizure, involving nearly 3.9 tonnes of cocaine reportedly concealed in a container carrying plastic waste from Ghana, had intensified concerns about the country’s exposure to international drug-trafficking networks. French authorities’ seizure has already triggered investigations in Ghana, with NACOC announcing arrests of suspects allegedly connected to the shipment. CDM argued that Ghana had spent decades building its reputation as a credible participant in international trade and diplomacy and that repeated drug-trafficking cases could undermine confidence in Ghanaian exports and transport routes. The organisation also raised concerns about the potential effect on ordinary Ghanaians, including travellers and businesses that may face greater scrutiny as a result of the cases. The group therefore called for decisive action to strengthen border controls, improve coordination among security agencies and establish accountability for any failures identified. It said a bipartisan parliamentary inquiry would provide an opportunity to examine the problem comprehensively and develop measures to protect Ghana’s international standing while ensuring that legitimate trade is not unduly affected.

items.title: Urgent – Kissidougou : neuf femmes périssent dans un accident après un mariage à Banian
items.description: Un grave accident de la circulation a fait neuf morts, dans la nuit du mercredi 23 au jeudi 24 septembre 2026, dans la sous-préfecture de Sangardo, à Kissidougou. Le drame s’est produit aux environs de 22 heures, dans la localité de Tonkelin, située à environ 18 kilomètres de la commune urbaine de Kissidougou. Selon les témoignages recueillis auprès des éléments de la Protection civile de Kissidougou intervenus sur les lieux, neuf personnes, toutes des femmes, ont perdu la vie dans cet accident. D’après les premières informations disponibles, le véhicule, de marque Opel, transportait une dizaine de personnes qui revenaient d’un mariage célébré dans la sous-préfecture de Banian, dans la préfecture de Faranah. Le véhicule aurait quitté la chaussée après avoir heurté un trou avant de terminer sa course dans un marigot situé à proximité d’un pont. Plusieurs passagers auraient alors été piégés dans le véhicule. Les premières informations recueillies sur place font état de décès par noyade. Les éléments de la Protection civile de Kissidougou ont mené plusieurs heures de recherches avant de parvenir à repêcher les neuf corps. Selon des proches des victimes, la jeune femme qui venait d’être mariée figure parmi les personnes décédées. Le marié ainsi que le chauffeur du véhicule auraient, quant à eux, survécu à l’accident. Les neuf dépouilles ont été transportées à l’hôpital préfectoral de Kissidougou, où elles se trouvent actuellement. Les circonstances précises de l’accident, ainsi que l’identité des victimes et le nombre exact de passagers à bord du véhicule, restent à préciser par les autorités compétentes.

items.title: Agriculture bio et labellisation : l’Algérie prépare ses futures normes avec l’UE
items.description: L’Algérie et l’Union européenne ont lancé mardi le projet de jumelage institutionnel pour mettre en place un « cadre normatif régissant l’agriculture biologique et la labellisation ». Avec ce projet, l’Algérie franchit un pas décisif pour compléter un maillon manquant de son agriculture : la mise en place de normes locales Bio et la labellisation de ses produits agricoles. Deux outils importants pour le développement de l’agriculture biologique et l’exportation des produits Bio. Jusqu’à présent, et faute de normes locales, les producteurs algériens de produits agricoles sont obligés de faire appel à des organismes étrangers pour la certification Bio de leurs produits. Le projet de jumelage est financé à hauteur d’un million d’euros par l’Union européenne pour une durée de 24 mois. Il associe les ministères de l’Agriculture italien et français avec l’appui de EUTALIA, organisme mandaté par l’Italie qui est le chef de file, chargé de la gestion administrative, a indiqué l’UE dans un communiqué. Normes Bio : l’Algérie s’appuie sur la France et l’Italie Les ministères français et italien de l’agriculture vont appuyer leur homologue algérien dans « l’élaboration du cadre réglementaire et de ses textes d’application, la définition des responsabilités des structures compétentes ainsi que l’organisation des procédures de contrôle et de certification. » Le projet financé par l’UE inclut aussi la formation des administrations et organismes appelés à « assurer le fonctionnement du futur dispositif national. » Le second volet de ce projet de jumelage concerne la création d’un Label Agricole de Qualité (LAQ) algérien. « L’action sera centrée sur les filières et leurs acteurs. Cinq filières pilotes seront accompagnées dans l’analyse des produits, l’identification de leurs spécificités et la définition des critères de qualité. Cette démarche conduira à l’élaboration participative de cinq cahiers des charges, en vue de leur soumission au Comité national de labellisation, tout en préparant les producteurs, transformateurs, organisations professionnelles et structures techniques à leur mise en œuvre », a précisé l’UE. L’article Agriculture bio et labellisation : l'Algérie prépare ses futures normes avec l'UE est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Lutte contre le financement du terrorisme : Le Niger encadre le transport physique de fonds
items.description: Le Gouvernement nigérien a décidé de mettre en place un dispositif plus adéquat et sécurisé pour encadrer le transport physique de fonds. Cette initiative s'inscrit dans le cadre de la lutte contre le terrorisme et son financement. L'information a été communiquée, le mardi 22 septembre 2026. Dans le cadre de la lutte contre le terrorisme et son financement, les Forces de défense et de sécurité nigériennes effectuent régulièrement des contrôles des mouvements importants de fonds sur le territoire national. Selon un communiqué du Secrétariat général du gouvernement, ces contrôles ont montré la nécessité de distinguer les mouvements de fonds réguliers de ceux présentant un caractère suspect. « C'est pourquoi le gouvernement a décidé de mettre en place un dispositif plus adéquat et sécurisé pour encadrer le transport physique de fonds », indique le communiqué. Désormais, au-delà des seuils maximaux fixés par la réglementation bancaire, le transport de fonds doit faire l'objet d'une déclaration préalable auprès des services compétents, conformément à l'arrêté conjoint n° 000428 portant régime spécial de transport de fonds. Lorsque les documents présentés sont réguliers et correspondent au montant des fonds transportés, l'opération pourra se poursuivre sans délai. En revanche, en cas d'absence de déclaration, d'incohérence des documents ou d'indices sérieux d'infraction, le contrôle et les procédures prévus par la législation en vigueur s'appliquent avec toute la rigueur requise. items.title: AI could transform productivity, economic policies- IMF
items.description: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) says Artificial Intelligence (AI) could significantly transform productivity, investment, labour markets and economic policy, while creating both opportunities and risks for workers, businesses and countries. The IMF said this in its 2026 Annual Report, entitled “Navigating a Precarious World”, released on Wednesday. The report said private-sector investment in AI could exceed two trillion dollars globally in 2026, according to some external estimates, making it one of the fastest-growing drivers of growth in recent years. According to the report, technology investments related to AI added an estimated 0.5 percentage point to United States’ Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth in 2025. It said productivity growth in the U.S. had also accelerated over the past several years, which might partly reflect the early impact of AI adoption. It further said as global spending shifted toward deploying AI across sectors, AI-driven productivity gains could accelerate across a broad range of industries and occupations. The IMF noted that Asia was actively pursuing AI opportunities, with Singapore ranking at the top of its AI Preparedness Index. It attributed Singapore’s position to its strong digital infrastructure, education and forward-looking regulation. “East Asia is a hub for chip manufacturing and design, while South-East Asia is building on its strength in manufacturing to move up the value chain as well.” However, the IMF warned that the rapid adoption of AI could create significant labour-market disruptions. It said policymakers, households and businesses were increasingly concerned about how AI would transform labour markets, including the possibility of job displacement and wage declines for some categories of workers. According to the report, IMF research showed that workers in jobs requiring AI-related skills earned more, but cities and regions with greater concentrations of such jobs were not experiencing overall job growth. It said workers with AI skills were benefiting, as were people in low-skill roles, such as restaurant staff members, who provided services to higher earners. “Left out are middle-skilled workers whose jobs are highly exposed to automation.” The IMF also warned of risks to businesses arising from heavy investment in AI, particularly where such investments were increasingly debt-financed. It said the returns from expensive AI investments could prove illusory, potentially leading to sharp reversals in equity valuations, wealth destruction and layoffs. Within the AI ecosystem, including hyperscalers building data centres and chipmakers, the IMF said circular financing arrangements could heighten systemic risks. It explained that such arrangements occurred when a small group of firms simultaneously acted as one another’s customers, investors and financiers. According to the report, this could increase the risk of problems in one firm cascading to others. The IMF said its Executive Board was regularly monitoring such risks through multilateral surveillance. It added that the fund was helping member countries navigate the rapidly evolving AI landscape through a suite of indexes covering national preparedness, skill readiness and skill imbalance. The indexes, it said, helped countries understand their strengths and weaknesses in areas such as workforce training, digital infrastructure, venture capital and regulation. The report said the indexes formed part of the IMF’s analysis of macro-critical issues relating to AI, including its impact on productivity and growth, labour markets and skills, inequality, financial markets, energy and climate. The fund said it was also helping countries draw lessons from those leading in AI-related policies and adapt them to their own circumstances. It said this enabled the IMF to provide tailored advice on structural policies, including how to help workers navigate AI-driven transitions and assess the technology’s potential implications for growth and inflation and monetary and fiscal policymaking. The IMF said it was also helping member countries guard against economic, financial stability and fiscal risks that could arise from an AI investment bust, particularly where public debt was already high. The fund said countries would need to guard against the risks associated with AI while continuing to pursue the potential benefits of the technology. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that beyond AI, the report identified rising public debt, trade reorientation and digital currencies as other major forces shaping the global economy. (NAN) The post AI could transform productivity, economic policies- IMF appeared first on Vanguard News .
